title: A Fish Was Filmed Over 5 Miles Deep Under 1,000 Times Normal Pressure

scenes.text: Scientists filmed a fish more than five miles underwater.
scenes.keywords: deep sea fish dark ocean submersible

scenes.text: It's a tiny juvenile snailfish, filmed in 2023 in a trench off Japan.
8,336 metres down. That's a new depth record for any fish ever filmed.
The pressure there is about 1,000 times what you feel at sea level.
It beat the old record, set in 2017, by 158 metres.
A fish, five miles down, under 1,000 times the pressure, and still swimming.

description:
In 2023 researchers filmed a juvenile snailfish at 8,336 metres in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench off Japan, the deepest fish ever recorded on camera.
The pressure there is around 1,000 times that at sea level. It beat the 2017 record by 158 metres.
What do you think is still lurking even deeper?
thumbnail_text: A FISH 5 MILES DOWN, ON CAMERA
first_comment: That is more than 27,000 feet down, nearly as deep as Mount Everest is tall. Would you ride a submersible that deep?
